title: Your right to protest and to associate
summary: You may assemble peacefully and associate with others, including forming or joining a political party, trade union, or other association.
body_plain: The Constitution guarantees the right to assemble freely and to associate with others. In particular, you may form or belong to any political party, trade union, or any other association for the protection of your interests. Peaceful assembly and protest are protected; the right is subject only to limits that are reasonably justifiable in a democratic society.
rights: You may assemble freely and peacefully with others (s.40).
You may form or join a political party, trade union, or other association (s.40).
do_list: Know the organisers and your route; document any interference.
dont_list: Do not assume a peaceful protest is illegal.
Do not engage in violence or destruction, which are not protected.
common_situations: You are attending, organising, observing, or reporting on a peaceful protest.
Officers order a crowd to disperse or begin arresting participants.
You are pressured to reveal the membership or communications of a lawful association.
words_to_use: This gathering is peaceful. What lawful direction are you giving us?
Am I being detained, or am I free to leave?
I will comply with a clear safety direction, but I do not consent to violence or an unlawful search.
if_violated: Move toward safety and avoid escalation; help others identify safe exits and emergency support.
Preserve original photographs or video with time and location information and record witnesses.
Document injuries, arrests, property damage, and instructions given by officials, then seek legal or human-rights assistance.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
citations.quote: Every person shall be entitled to assemble freely and associate with other persons, and in particular he may form or belong to any political party, trade union or any other association for the protection of his interests.
